pr_title: Fix #41413 by using a specific purpose for direct uploads
pr_body:
### Summary

Fixes #41413 by using a specific `purpose` when generating the `signed_id` of `ActiveStorage::Blob`s for direct uploads. I think it would be important to fix it since a user should have the right to permanently delete blobs uploaded by them.

Before this change, the attack described in the issue was possible just by knowing the `signed_id` of a Blob. And the `signed_id` is present in shareable URLs, so it's expected that some people know some `signed_id`s.

After this change, the attack described would only be possible if intercepting the response of the direct uploads controller. Which wouldn't be possible just because of SSL.

This is a **breaking change** since it'd break any app that performs any `find_signed` call in the context of direct uploads because it's assuming the purpose would be `blob_id`.

cc @georgeclaghorn
pr_comments: I don’t feel comfortable breaking already-issued signed IDs for upgrading apps. I think we need to add a config option, default it to on for new apps, and deprecate the old behavior.

Sounds fair to me @georgeclaghorn. I just updated the PR making the change be configurable based on how I found it being done in other parts of Rails. I still have some concerns:
- This approach still has a non-zero downtime during migration. To have no downtime during the migration we'll need to have the `find_or_build_blob` method find by any of the two purposes for some time. Not sure it's worth it though..
- For people that monkey patched the ActiveStorage controllers (e.g. for security purposes) they MUST update the controller when upgrading.
- For people that used `ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(..., purpose: :blob_id)` or similar for direct uploads flows they MUST update their code to use the new purpose.

Any thoughts on the above?

On the other hand, the good thing is that if this is included for Rails 7 people by default will probably be extra cautious (for being a major version upgrade)

> This approach still has a non-zero downtime during migration. To have no downtime during the migration we'll need to have the find_or_build_blob method find by any of the two purposes for some time. Not sure it's worth it though..

Yeah, this is what I had in mind (and I do think it needs to be seamless). Generate signed IDs with the new purpose unconditionally. The flag controls whether we accept the old purpose as a fallback. Warn in an `after_initialize` hook if configured to accept the old purpose.

Hi @gmcgibbon I don't want to bug you, but I don't know who to ping now that George left the team. Are you able to help moving this security fix forward or otherwise can you point me to the right person? Thanks 🙌

If I'm understanding this correctly, the default behavior is still to sign by `:blob_id` but we provide a configuration flag for users to migrate their applications once they're running on 7.0.

Are we setting the flag to default to `:private_id` for newly generated apps?

> If I'm understanding this correctly, the default behavior is still to sign by `:blob_id` but we provide a configuration flag for users to migrate their applications once they're running on 7.0.

That's correct. 

> Are we setting the flag to default to `:private_id` for newly generated apps?

Newly generated apps (once Rails 7 is out) will load 7.0 defaults and be affected by https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/41433/files#diff-9f26e965e7e2a6842bd6ea755924a621038bc9dd8d63cfa6b34092aa32ede02cR221
@gmcgibbon Could you give this another look too plz? :bow:

Given that it's a major version change a lot of apps will want to run 6.1 and 7.0 in production at the same time - is that scenario covered by the `:private_id_with_falback` option or will they need to keep the setting at `:blob_id` for the duration of that phase. If the latter we'd want to point that out in the upgrading guide/changelog.

Can we also add some configuration tests similar to other new framework default tests in `railties/test/application/configuration_test.rb` - thanks.

Thank you for your contributions.

issue_context.title: ActiveStorage blobs can be attached using their "displayable" signed IDs
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

ActiveStorage blobs currently use signed IDs. The purpose however is always the same (blob_id). When uploading a Blob through the direct_upload endpoint, a user gets the same signed ID for a Blob as the one that is later used for attaching a Blob to a model through Attached - see https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/bddb2c9b193c976dbe6a9a1358479d1792931986/activestorage/app/controllers/active_storage/direct_uploads_controller.rb#L18

Since the signed blob ID is the same as the one used for later retrieving a blob (even for a small period of time, since the purpose of the signature is the same), the following attack can be performed:

* Alice uploads a PDF document and shares a link to a page with it with Bob
* Mallory manages to view that page for whatever reason
* Mallory examines the source page and copies the signed ID of the blob on that page
* Mallory then uses her account on the same service and supplies the signed ID of the blob in a form POST request which would perform file attachment and create a reference to the blob in their account too.

At that stage, the Blob in the database would have more referencing Attachments since an Attachment would be generated allowing Mallory to have full access to the Blob in their account on the service. This would also prevent the Blob from being garbage-collected if Alice decides to remove it from "her" attachment. At first glance, I see the following possible impact:

* An attacker can link attachments stored on the service into the model objects belonging to the attacker, even though they weren't uploaded by the attacker
* An attacker can "increase refcount" for Blobs and thus prevent those blobs from being deleted from the application once there are no Attachments referencing them from records belonging to accounts that did have access.

Mitigation would possibly require using a different signature purpose for direct uploading / attaching than the rest of the ActiveStorage operations. An alternative would be to blend the user account identifier into the signature for upload, so that an account may only use signed IDs which were generated for them / on their behalf (Since Rails does not provide authorization out-of-the-box I don't see that likely but might be possible).

### Expected behavior

It is only possible to attach a blob to a record using a signed ID if that signed ID was issued to you for the purpose of upload (proof-of-work).

### Actual behavior

Signed IDs are used interchangeably and attaching by any user is possible, even if the user was not the original uploader.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 5.x -6.x

**Ruby version**: any relevant version for framework versions mentioned above

review_comments:
I'm hesitant to believe that this code path will only ever be used for direct uploads. Users could try attaching by signed ID via database seeding for example. There may also be legitimate use-cases for using one blob for multiple attachment relations.

How can we conditionalize this further to only check when the attachable is meant to be a direct upload? The fact that we had to turn on the new feature for all of our one + many attachment tests is an indicator that we're breaking contract on other code paths.

Hey @gmcgibbon, we gave some thought to your comments and we think that breaking the API is inevitable if we are to fix the security vulnerability but we should also contemplate older apps running on production right now. To consider these older apps we agree this should be a configuration to allow them to keep their current behavior and since, as you mentioned, the path is more widely used we thought about renaming the purpose from `:direct_upload` to `:private_id`.

The configuration will be set to use `:private_id` by default on new Rails 7+ apps prioritizing security and `:blob_id` on older ones. To ensure a smooth migration we also included a `:private_id_with_fallback` value which will sign direct uploads with `:private_id` but accept both `:blob_id` and `:private_id` until they change it to the more secure mode `:private_id`. We've included these changes along with an explanation in the CHANGELOG and migration guides as per @zzak's comments :)
